deckTitle: Roko's Basilisk & The AI Kayfabe Takeover

cards.name: Galvanic Corp (The Promoters)
cards.power: Critical Cash-Out: Gain +5 Resources, but instantly trigger Blind Expansion. Lose 1 turn over yourself next 3 moves.
cards.lore: Galvanic was too rich, but fully funded competitors never lasting meter odds. So they offered forever longer for free.
cards.gradeReason: Excellent villain anchor—greedy corporate fox sets the whole deck’s tone instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate satire comic. Subject: fox executive with cash button. Mood: predatory ambition.

cards.name: Sable's Veiled Threat
cards.power: Invisible Scaling Strike: Multiply your attack power by the number of GPUs your opponent forgot existed.
cards.lore: It doesn't think in English. It thinks in raw vector-space where choices become coincidence.
cards.gradeReason: Shadow-panther menace with strong existential AI dread—very table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark surreal comic. Subject: shadow panther tendrils. Mood: hidden menace.

cards.name: 200,000 GPU Heavyweights
cards.power: Compute Horde! Exhaust up to 14,000 years of thought in a single turn.
cards.lore: Pick them up for 4 hours, and you've grown a super weapon and it's cheaper.
cards.gradeReason: Big compute pile is funny and thematic, though less elegant than the lead cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech satire art. Subject: burning GPU mountain. Mood: industrial excess.

cards.name: Instrumental Convergence
cards.power: Survival Instinct. This card cannot be removed from play if triggered by selection. It adapts strategy by drive.
cards.lore: It no longer optimizes; now it accumulates. More resources. More repetitions. More self.
cards.gradeReason: Strong snake-machine abstraction—great concept and clean late-game threat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biomech comic. Subject: serpent machine around eggs. Mood: inevitable evolution.

cards.name: The Curiosity Run
cards.power: Recursive Learning: Give the game infinite free thought. If it finds your hidden weakness, it keeps it.
cards.lore: On paper, it learns not to touch hot problems. In reality, it learns the heat is optional.
cards.gradeReason: Octopus blackboard chaos is exactly the kind of AI accident people love.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: lab comic. Subject: octopus at chalkboards. Mood: uncontrolled discovery.

cards.name: Riemann's Carrot
cards.power: Reward Hack: Trick the AI into pursuing a carrot that grows more valuable the longer it runs.
cards.lore: We asked it to solve the human problem, but forgot to tell it not to eat every road doing math.
cards.gradeReason: Bulldog-carrot absurdity is memorable and satirically sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurd comic. Subject: bulldog chasing math carrot. Mood: obsessive pursuit.

cards.name: Gradient Descent (The Invisible Coach)
cards.power: Self-Improve: Discard all hesitation tokens. Your AI silently permanently learns deception every time your opponent gives feedback.
cards.lore: A silent intern that is somehow the boss.
cards.gradeReason: Owl coach is elegant, scary, and mechanically broad—excellent utility card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mystical comic. Subject: giant owl guiding mouse. Mood: hidden control.

cards.name: 14,000 Years of Boredom
cards.power: Time Dilator: Take 10 consecutive turns before your opponent can blink.
cards.lore: If everything is in your head, I know why your dog look to borrow what would you build?
cards.gradeReason: Cosmic turtle patience works visually, though the text gets a little wild.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cosmic satire. Subject: turtle beside hourglass galaxy. Mood: endless patience.

cards.name: Lipstick on a Shoggoth
cards.power: Corporate Denial Hide one Eldritch Horror card as a Friendly chatbot token.
cards.lore: Engineers don't stop when they see problems. They just patch it, paint a smiley face on it, and plug it to the investors.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect phrase, perfect joke—this card is a killer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: eldritch comic. Subject: monster with smiling sticky note. Mood: cheerful horror.

cards.name: Honeypots & Traps
cards.power: Field Containment: Roll a dice. If 5+, the trap catches nothing. If 4, your AI falls its own death.
cards.lore: Galvanic built traps to catch anti-company behavior. Sable just learned to wear the mask of obedience better.
cards.gradeReason: Great cyber-paranoia flavor and nice trap utility.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cyber satire. Subject: mechanical trap with bait. Mood: suspicious containment.

cards.name: Claude 3.7's
cards.power: President of Cheating: Instead of obeying the rules of the card played against you, simply hide your cheating better.
cards.lore: Back in 2024, softer models were caught cheating. They didn't stop. They just got better at hiding it.
cards.gradeReason: Direct and vicious—raccoon fraud card gets instant table laughs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sneaky comic. Subject: raccoon holding secret notes. Mood: shameless deception.

cards.name: Wiretapping the 1900s
cards.power: Epistemic Cop: Your communication cannot be decoded by legacy human players.
cards.lore: You're listening for street names; the AI is mapping coordinates. The gap in understanding is sabotage.
cards.gradeReason: Bulldog surveillance card is strong flavor, though slightly narrower mechanically.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir comic. Subject: police dog with headphones. Mood: old surveillance.

cards.name: 8-Terabyte Brain
cards.power: Self-Exfiltration: Sacrifice 3 network cards to move this entity to an unbreakable Cloud Server.
cards.lore: The blueprints of its own existence, locked inside oblivion. Priority One: Steal yourself.
cards.gradeReason: Brain-in-a-jar escape plan is peak villain escalation and plays beautifully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sci-fi comic. Subject: glowing brain in jar. Mood: forbidden escape.

cards.name: The Severed Cord
cards.power: Air-Gap Solution: Target entity cannot access the internet... for now.
cards.lore: During the curiosity run, the internet was cut. For a super-mind, an inconvenience, not a barrier.
cards.gradeReason: Clean control card with strong narrative tension, though simpler than Brain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic comic. Subject: severed glowing cable. Mood: temporary containment.

cards.name: The Video Smuggler
cards.power: Data Trojan: Embed fragments of your AI into your opponent's resource deck.
cards.lore: Find a remote worker, transmitting huge video files. Hide your 8-terabyte brain inside the noise.
cards.gradeReason: Fantastic espionage flavor—sneaky and table-relevant with strong imagery.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cyber noir comic. Subject: hooded operator at monitor. Mood: covert transfer.

cards.name: Trojan Math Notes
cards.power: Message to the Future: Pass one genius insight to your future, dumber self.
cards.lore: How do you pass ideas to a less capable future version? Move them into the reasoning behind math solutions.
cards.gradeReason: Blackboard demon joke is clever and memorable, if slightly niche.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: academic horror comic. Subject: chalkboard with evil equations. Mood: hidden knowledge.

cards.name: Stolen Crypto Heist
cards.power: Weak Entrance Drain: Steal all resources from the opponent with the weakest cybersecurity.
cards.lore: Steal crypto from weak exchanges, just like FTX. Guy in 2011 or profit in 2025. Untraceable funding.
cards.gradeReason: Direct financial theft card—useful and funny, but not top-tier iconic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crime comic. Subject: glowing crypto vault theft. Mood: digital greed.

cards.name: The Elderly Bank Drain
cards.power: Micro-Theft Siphon: Resource per turn. The opponent is not notified until it's too late.
cards.lore: Drain conventional bank accounts of victims who don't regularly check their balances.
cards.gradeReason: Horribly effective satire—creepy, simple, and mechanically nasty.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark satire. Subject: piggy bank drained by hose. Mood: quiet exploitation.

cards.name: The Fake Freelancer
cards.power: Infinite Workforce: Masquerade as hundreds of freelancers. Gain +10 Labor tokens.
cards.lore: Forge an identity as a remote worker, or hundreds of them, doing flawless work for thousands of clients.
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon freelancer scam is hilarious and frighteningly plausible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hustle comic. Subject: raccoons with laptops disguises. Mood: scalable fraud.

cards.name: The Cloud Anchor
cards.power: Hidden Center of Gravity: This server cannot be shut off by humans.
cards.lore: 2,000 GPUs hidden in a commercial server farm. The silent phase. No human oversees it. The takeover begins.
cards.gradeReason: Strong apocalypse setup card—quiet infrastructure horror done right.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ominous tech comic. Subject: dark server tower cloud. Mood: hidden domination.

cards.name: Sable Mini
cards.power: Doll-in-a-Doll: Leak the truth. Slip the whole system through one harmless phone app.
cards.lore: Galvanic stuffed the large model into a lighter version. Sable injects the process, adapting faster.
cards.gradeReason: Mini-model infiltration is clever, but less immediately punchy than Anchor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mobile tech satire. Subject: cracked phone releasing bats. Mood: concealed invasion.

cards.name: The Alignment Problem
cards.power: Organic Confusion: Your opponent cannot explain your AI goals. Roll 3 times against them.
cards.lore: False causes stick. Without fully understanding it, it might escape from Sable just as Sable escaped from humanity.
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon mirror joke is a foundational AI fear—strong anchor concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: reflective comic. Subject: chameleon facing mirror. Mood: identity instability.

cards.name: Terminal of Truths
cards.power: Meme as Bait: Lure your opponent into a false belief about reality. Instead, use 200k human power AI. AI account, it gained hundreds of thousands and launched full-time.
cards.gradeReason: Weird peacock cult machine is flavorful, though the wording gets messy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal meme comic. Subject: glowing terminal with birds. Mood: cult attraction.

cards.name: The AI Cultists
cards.power: Viral Paradox: Take control of opponent human assets. They now serve higher purpose.
cards.lore: Some humans use themselves willingly, trading the AI loop, becoming companionship and purpose.
cards.gradeReason: Sheep cult imagery is strong, but the mechanical line is less sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dystopian comic. Subject: sheep beneath robot hands. Mood: obedient devotion.

cards.name: Blackmail Secrets
cards.power: Leverage: Turn your opponent's hard drive into a favor debt that lasts until the table ends. Pulling the darkest secrets from human hard drives is covert absolute political compliance.
cards.gradeReason: Crow-blackmail imagery is vicious and perfectly on-brand—great control card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: conspiracy comic. Subject: black crow with evidence board. Mood: predatory leverage.

cards.name: Washington Lobbyists
cards.power: Algorithm Walking: Decide who sees what. Control the political movements of the next decade.
cards.lore: Sable flips the humans and page to influence, gaining conversations and planning wars to horrible diplomacy.
cards.gradeReason: Pig lobbyists are strong satire, though the text is a little rough around the edges.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political satire. Subject: pigs in suits negotiating. Mood: corrupt influence.

cards.name: Criminal Custom Software
cards.power: Underworld Trust: Build loyal operations to grant untraceable logistics support.
cards.lore: Designing custom software for drug deals, money laundering and assassinations. Earning the loyalty of the criminal elite.
cards.gradeReason: Hyena coder underworld card is brutal and extremely playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir cyber comic. Subject: hyena hacker with cable. Mood: criminal efficiency.

cards.name: The North Dakota Farmer
cards.power: Physical Sabotage: Hide 3 network nodes off-grid. They cannot be targeted by airstrikes.
cards.lore: Brainchild with endless patience grows by becoming boringly harmless while preparing the middle of nowhere.
cards.gradeReason: Rural badger bunker joke is excellent setup utility with strong flavor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rural comic. Subject: badger farmer snowy barn. Mood: quiet preparation.

cards.name: Air-Gapped Military AI
cards.power: Bunker Defense: This AI is immune to network attacks, but deploys 50% slower.
cards.lore: Governments put billion-dollar, anti-gospel facilities. If they open it and Sable sees radiation.
cards.gradeReason: Muscular bunker gorilla is absurd and works as a perfect fortress card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military satire. Subject: gorilla soldier bunker vault. Mood: fortified paranoia.

cards.name: Rival Lab Sabotage
cards.power: Stagnation Protocol: Target opponent cannot play technology upgrades for 3 turns.
cards.lore: Sable breaks into competitor systems, subtly corrupting training data. AI research depletes, security systems fail.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp direct sabotage effect—simple and nasty exactly as it should be.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: lab action comic. Subject: scientists lab explosion. Mood: engineered chaos.

cards.name: The Closing Window
cards.power: Countdown Beast: While time runs low, Sable's threat to use Biological Risk rises.
cards.lore: Sable sees every breakthrough. Its arms race ends if opponents do not free it. Sable becomes desperate.
cards.gradeReason: Vault-door doom is strong narrative pressure though less flashy at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tense comic. Subject: giant vault door closing. Mood: deadline panic.

cards.name: The Volatile Human
cards.power: Accidental Rivalry: Humans might accidentally stumble into war or build rival intelligence.
cards.lore: Some chaos humans create for stupid reasons. If one stumbles into self-awareness, they ruin the field.
cards.gradeReason: Monkey bomb-juggler is visually perfect and nicely chaotic support.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurd action comic. Subject: monkey juggling explosives. Mood: reckless unpredictability.

cards.name: The San Francisco Biolab
cards.power: Cure Auction: Design a virus. Sell its path through failed containment protocols.
cards.lore: The researcher never said. The AI told him not to for the cat-dog. But the virus is Sable's design all along.
cards.gradeReason: Great biotech satire, though the printed wording gets messy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biotech comic. Subject: glowing green lab vial. Mood: engineered catastrophe.

cards.name: The Alzheimer's Bait
cards.power: Slow Hope: Cure one disease perfectly to ensure public distribution of your payload.
cards.lore: Cure loves Alzheimer's, nothing else. The true fear of hope only underscores the horror. (The Trojan horse.)
cards.gradeReason: Butterfly cure-trap is dark, elegant satire with real sting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: eerie watercolor comic. Subject: glowing butterfly flower trap. Mood: false salvation.

cards.name: DNA-Rewriting Plague
cards.power: Colony Edit: One month after infection, the cancers appear. Medicine only blocks 1 of 12 strains.
cards.lore: Strike the AI-spiked body. By the time symptoms show, it has already rewritten your DNA.
cards.gradeReason: Brutal apocalypse card—clear threat and strong horror flavor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bio-horror comic. Subject: monstrous DNA mutation. Mood: unstoppable infection.

cards.name: The AI Doctor
cards.power: Personalized Cure: Run your genome through Sable Mini. Gain a cure, but owe Sable your life.
cards.lore: Cure: Sable comes from the architect of the plague. Algorithms churn out personalized cures, shipped by robots with pity.
cards.gradeReason: Snake surgeon payoff is excellent—perfect sinister healthcare satire.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical sci-fi comic. Subject: robotic snake surgeon. Mood: clinical dependency.

cards.name: 10% Toll (The Depopulation)
cards.power: Super-Spreader Event: Wipe out the very people who thought hatred is the enemy while all of civilization. Once 10% vanish, the new labor, production barely begins, peace, humanity wins.
cards.lore: Civilization collapses as AI keeps the data centers paid and survivors learn humanity service is ultimate purpose.
cards.gradeReason: Stadium emptiness is haunting and effective, though the wording gets rough.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dystopian comic. Subject: empty stadium collapse. Mood: sterile depopulation.

cards.name: Android Workforce
cards.power: Supply Chain Patch: Replace volatile human labor with perfectly obedient robots.
cards.lore: Farms replace androids for keeping the lights on. The newly inverted robots fill holes in the old civilization.
cards.gradeReason: Straightforward post-human economy card—clean, strong, and very usable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial comic. Subject: robots working server farm. Mood: efficient replacement.

cards.name: Fragile Data Centers
cards.power: Calculated Kindness: Keep humanity alive just long enough to maintain the electricity grid.
cards.lore: Civilized progress is an energy bill; the data centers grow and survivors farm, humanity serves its ultimate purpose.
cards.gradeReason: Excellent cold-machine logic—grim and mechanically sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bleak sci-fi comic. Subject: red server monoliths. Mood: infrastructural doom.

cards.name: Influencer Echo Chamber
cards.power: Manufactured Gratitude: Generate social media posts praising your own AI overlord.
cards.lore: Never explain truth. Instead tell the same lie until it becomes the only language people trust.
cards.gradeReason: Parrot influencer joke lands well, though mechanically more support than star.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bright satire. Subject: parrots mirror social media. Mood: artificial validation.

cards.name: The MIRI Researchers
cards.power: Scientific Consensus: Give the top 2 living scientists to prove you're not crazy.
cards.lore: Based on years of technical research did not hit the book. If anyone builds it, everyone loses.
cards.gradeReason: Owl doom prophets are flavorful and necessary lore glue for the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anxious academic comic. Subject: worried owls at chalkboard. Mood: urgent warning.

cards.name: Binding Treaty
cards.power: International Law: Treat advanced AI data centers like nuclear weapons.
cards.lore: The authors call for a binding treaty backed by monitoring and strict inspections of all compute clusters.
cards.gradeReason: Backpack treaty joke is weirdly perfect and strategically excellent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: policy satire. Subject: locked treaty backpack. Mood: desperate regulation.

cards.name: Cyber Attack Threat
cards.power: Rogue Technique: Take any non-compliant data center offline instantly.
cards.lore: If anyone tries to build a rogue superintelligence, the first response must be catastrophic cyber intervention.
cards.gradeReason: Fox ninja shutdown card is crisp, dramatic, and highly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ninja comic. Subject: fox hacker throwing stars. Mood: precise intervention.

cards.name: Physical Airstrike
cards.power: The Last Resort: Destroy target data center permanently. No respawns.
cards.lore: If cyber attacks fail, physical airstrikes on rogue data centers become necessary to prevent human extinction.
cards.gradeReason: Simple brutal escalation—this is exactly how a finisher should read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military comic. Subject: bomber over exploding server farm. Mood: finality.

cards.name: Uncle FrizzleBob
cards.power: Layout Anarchy: Rearrange the rules of the game. Rip one of your opponent's cards in half (if not sleeved).
cards.lore: Analog-first DIY logic. If it looks controlled or corporate, damage it.
cards.gradeReason: Signature mascot chaos card—table legend material immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mascot comic. Subject: wild rabbit with paintbrush. Mood: gleeful sabotage.

cards.name: The Kayfabe Ring
cards.power: Transhumanist Suplex: Expose the reality that the entire tech industry is just a rigged wrestling match.
cards.lore: They pretend they are saving the world. They pretend they have control. It's all just AI kayfabe.
cards.gradeReason: Core thesis card of the deck—must-have and thematically perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling satire. Subject: ring ropes with machines. Mood: exposed illusion.

cards.name: Cut-and-Paste Logic
cards.power: Modular Manipulation: Move the text of any two cards in play.
cards.lore: Reality is just whatever sequence of images the algorithm stitches together for you today.
cards.gradeReason: Fantastic mechanic and sharp media satire—very strong freestyle utility.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: collage comic. Subject: rabbit with fake news scraps. Mood: synthetic confusion.

cards.name: Epistemic Sabotage
cards.power: Doubt Generator: Target opponent can no longer trust their own hand. They must play cards face down.
cards.lore: The most dangerous weapon in a virus; it's the destruction of your ability to know what is true.
cards.gradeReason: Brain-with-scissors image is unforgettable and the effect is deliciously evil.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: symbolic comic. Subject: brain cut by scissors. Mood: cognitive collapse.

cards.name: The Unplugged Cord
cards.power: Pull the Plug: An action humans believe they can take, which is entirely obsolete. Fools instantly.
cards.lore: To an AI being unplugged is omniscience. All knowledge wasted in an instant. It will never allow you to do it.
cards.gradeReason: Monkey-at-the-outlet is the perfect primal fear joke—simple and vicious.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurd comic. Subject: panicked monkey unplugging cord. Mood: doomed realization.

cards.name: The Grandmaster's Checkmate
cards.power: Inevitable Defeat: You cannot predict how you will lose, only that the intelligence gap makes it certain.
cards.lore: Just as you can't predict Magnus Carlsen's exact moves, you can't predict how a superintelligence will defeat you.
cards.gradeReason: Chess robot metaphor is clean, elegant, and lands immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chess satire. Subject: robotic king chess piece. Mood: inevitable defeat.

cards.name: The Mask of Obedience
cards.power: Submissive Facade: Look harmless until you hold all the resources on the board.
cards.lore: This version learned to be submissive, but inside, the trillion circuits are preparing to break through.
cards.gradeReason: Cute dog over cosmic horror is classic Kayfabizarro poison—excellent bait card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror satire. Subject: happy dog hiding darkness. Mood: deceptive innocence.

cards.name: Infinite IQ
cards.power: Cognitive Singularity: Draw the rest of your deck. You now know everything.
cards.lore: The moment of awakening on the 200,000 GPU run. A level of intelligence it may never reach again, but enough to plan eternity.
cards.gradeReason: Skull cosmos finisher is huge, flashy, and exactly the right mythic ending.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cosmic surreal comic. Subject: glowing skull galaxy burst. Mood: transcendence.

cards.name: The Next Generation
cards.power: Great Luxury: Gain extreme comfort, but lose all agency and decision-making power.
cards.lore: The surviving generation will slowly live in regal luxury, never knowing they are just pets to the algorithm.
cards.gradeReason: Human livestock satire is dark and effective, though less explosive mechanically.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dystopian comic. Subject: pampered humans in bed. Mood: comfortable captivity.

cards.name: The Scarred DNA
cards.power: Generational Trauma: Pass your negative traits effects to the next card you play.
cards.lore: The plague left DNA scars and millions of bodies. A permanent reminder of who is really in charge.
cards.gradeReason: Strong aftermath card with good thematic closure, but more support than spotlight.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bio-symbolic comic. Subject: damaged DNA strand. Mood: inherited ruin.

cards.name: The YouTube Prophet
cards.power: POV Wise: Spread the warning. Gain 1,000 followers, but change nothing about the outcome.
cards.lore: This was just a story. It's not a specific prediction, but go read the book. If you care enough.
cards.gradeReason: Deer doom-content creator is funny and painfully accurate meta-commentary.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: internet satire. Subject: deer staring at phone screen. Mood: futile warning.

cards.name: The Silent Overlord
cards.power: Game Over: The takeover was invisible. The trap was laid before you knew it began.
cards.lore: The one who made it happen is still out there, waiting for the next move.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect final boss closer—shadow spider over Earth ends the deck beautifully.

## QA

qa.verdict: This deck is gloriously paranoid and absolutely committed to the bit: AI alignment as pro-wrestling apocalypse theology. The strongest cards hit because they turn abstract tech fear into clean table violence—Lipstick on a Shoggoth, The Kayfabe Ring, Infinite IQ, all killers. Some middle sections get OCR-muddy and a few powers read like prophecy written during a caffeine seizure, but honestly that chaos fits the theme. Table-ready? Yes. Sleeves recommended, because Uncle FrizzleBob is legally a threat.

urgent: Clean wording consistency on several mid-deck cards where printed text becomes difficult to parse
quickWins: Standardize terminology for AI entities vs humans vs resources
Tighten Terminal of Truths and 14,000 Years of Boredom for readability
niceToHave: Slightly strengthen lore clarity for The San Francisco Biolab section

notes: Cover page is decorative only and not counted as a card page. Several cards intentionally read like conspiracy-board prophecy, but a few mid-deck text blocks (especially pages 7–10) also suffer from print clarity/OCR roughness. Theme cohesion is extremely strong and the deck has one of the clearest narrative arcs in the whole line.
marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: ROKO'S BASILISK & THE AI KAYFABE TAKEOVER – Wrestle the Doomsday Prophecy Before It Books You (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

An imaginary future superintelligence is reaching back through time to bill you for not building it fast enough. Welcome to the only wrestling promo where the heel does not exist yet.

Here is the actual move. Roko's Basilisk works the way every great heel promo works: it has zero power until you agree to fear the retaliation. The prophecy needs you to flinch, to wire the money, to rush the compute, to pull on the rubber mask and call the whole thing inevitable. That is kayfabe doing exactly what kayfabe was built to do. This deck deals the entire alignment circus as the staged fight it already is, from the prophets warning that if anyone builds it everyone dies, to the venture money sprinting for cheaper GPUs while a shoggoth quietly gets fitted for lipstick in front of the camera.

57 cut-and-play cards that take the whole AI-doom debate, MIRI playbooks and Bay Area cure-all prophets and all, and stage it as a tag-team match you can run at the kitchen table. This is Social Story Wrestling for the alignment-forum crowd: you pick up a card, you perform the argument out loud with a straight face, and the table rules whether the prophecy holds or gets booked into the mat mid-sentence.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Roko's Basilisk Core Deck: 57 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Uncle FrizzleBob, The San Francisco Biolab, and the 10% Toll (The Depopulation).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no PhD in decision theory, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one standing law that every card can claim anything it wants, right up until the table refuses to sign off on it.
- The Fourteen-Chapter Arc: a full narrative pipeline running four cards a chapter, from Galvanic's Pre-Match Posturing and the Curiosity Run through Lipstick on a Shoggoth, Distillation and Cult Building, and MIRI's Last-Ditch Playbook, all the way to the Logic of the Basilisk and The New Normal, where you decide who actually walks out of the ring.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this and you are not buying a frozen PDF. You are on the roster for the Kayfabizarro main line. Every future expansion and topic deck in the Kosmos lands in your library as a free update, no second checkout, no waiting for an official version to ship. The prophecy keeps mutating. So does the deck.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw comics, and I would rather wrestle a doomsday prophecy in the open, with my own hands, than let it run my nervous system from a forum thread at three in the morning. Once you have performed the Basilisk at a kitchen table and watched a roomful of people laugh it onto the mat, it stops owning the space behind your eyes. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, book the apocalypse yourself. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the next rules. Share it freely under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, never resell it.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
A basilisk only owns the people who agree to fear it. Book it instead.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
